name: Kalshi BTC venue repricing lag
description: A qualifying spot move is a spot-reference midpoint simple return of at least move_threshold_bps measured over a rolling 5-second lookback on the spot-reference series — the return between the current price and the oldest sample still within the window (both the 5-second lookback and the 10 bps threshold are research defaults). repricing_lag_ms is the time from that move to the first Kalshi quote change — a nonzero change in either outcome midpoint (affirmative or negative) — answering it; staleness_ms is the time the currently unanswered move has waited, measured from the move itself. state is lagging while a qualifying move is unanswered and current otherwise. A qualifying move is armed on entry into the qualifying state; while a move is unanswered a further qualifying return does not re-arm, so the lag measures the venue response to the first unanswered move. Until the first move has been answered the instance is not ready and publishes no_qualifying_move (upstream_measurement_unavailable is published only before the spot reference and a venue quote have both been observed). This deliberately does not model the implied magnitude of the venue response; that is the fair_up_probability lane. move_threshold_bps defaults to 10. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
